sections.title: Before reading: study Chapter 9 in How to read. An open door stops the large chest

segments.text: 架上有水，卷濕。寧取卷，還卷。人持卷，持帙。安持燈，客持書。
屋有二門。此門在屋前，門外有雨。彼門在屋後，門後有屋，屋乾。
寧開彼門，立門前。人視彼屋，見架。架乾，架上無水。安、寧、客，三人視架。
安持燈，至彼屋。客在此屋，持書。安視架上，寧視架下。彼屋無水，架乾。
安還，指彼門。
安：「彼屋有處。」
segments.speaker: char-an

segments.text: 寧視卷，人持卷。客視帙，帙乾。
此屋有二箱。一箱大，一箱小。大箱空，小箱空。客視箱，人持卷。
大箱有蓋。蓋裂，蓋上有水。安視蓋，寧視水。人不移卷，客不移書。
寧持繩。此繩短，彼繩長。寧移此繩。此繩在屋中。寧更繩，取彼繩。繩在箱下，安持繩。
安有力，寧持繩。安移箱，寧持繩。箱至門前，箱不過門。安止，寧止。

segments.text: 人還卷，寧持卷。人持帙，帙有印。寧移卷。卷在箱中，帙在箱外。

grammar.title: 此箱大，彼箱小。
grammar.rule: 箱｜大；門｜小。此繩｜長；彼繩｜短。
grammar.note_en:
A qualitative predicate states a property about its subject. In 箱重 xiāng zhòng, “The chest is heavy,” 箱 names what we describe and 重 supplies the description. Chinese does not need an extra verb meaning is here. 箱輕 xiāng qīng means “The chest is light in weight,” not “bright”: the lamp is 明 míng. 長 cháng means long in physical length, not zhǎng grow. 短 duǎn means short. Keep these selected meanings distinct from the different readings or later senses of the same graphs.

Compare by putting two explicit statements side by side: 此箱大，彼箱小, “This chest is large; that one is small.” 此繩長，彼繩短 means “This cord is long; that cord is short.” There is no inserted than word. The properties and referents give the contrast. The finite labels 大箱 dà xiāng, “large chest,” and 小箱 xiǎo xiāng, “small chest,” distinguish the two already established chests. In 箱大 the quality follows its subject and makes a statement; in 大箱 it precedes this noun and helps name the object. These two labels extend the earlier book labels; they are not permission to form arbitrary adjective-noun expressions.

三 sān is three. 三人 means three people; 二門 means two doors. Put the studied numeral before the studied noun: 三架, “three shelves,” 三卷, “three fascicles.” This is the current literary quantity pattern, not a lesson in modern spoken classifiers. In 安、寧、客，三人視架, An, Ning and the guest are the three counted people. The separate 人 outside that counted group is the near-gate reader. Do not turn every occurrence of the graph 人 into that reader's name.

空 kōng means empty of stored contents here: 箱空, “The chest is empty.” It is not the later sky/open-space sense. The same small chest first contains the guest's encased book and surname sheet. After unloading, 箱空 explicitly establishes its empty return. It later carries the wet fascicle. Count two loaded journeys by these different contents and their unloading; an empty crossing is not another loaded journey, and two people on one crossing do not make two journeys.

更 gēng takes the named object that is replaced: 寧更繩, “Ning changes the cord,” and 更箱, “change the chest.” Adjacent clauses establish the new selection. This is not gèng more. 再 zài goes before a repeated action: 安再移箱, “An moves the chest again,” and 寧再視葉, “Ning looks at the leaves again.” An earlier occurrence must actually be available; 再 is not a generic then. Its selected again reading does not introduce a journey counter or mean that every event described has occurred exactly twice.

過 guò is pass a physical landmark. 安過門 means “An passes the doorway.” 箱過門 means “The chest passes through the doorway.” In 箱不過門, “The chest does not pass through the doorway,” the open door, attempted movement and 箱大，門小 contrast establish the particular obstruction. It is not a hidden ability modal. The text need not claim that no turning, dismantling or alteration could ever solve it. Force is not the same as fit: 力 lì is strength, as in 安有力, “An has strength,” while the large chest still fails the doorway.

箱 xiāng is a chest. 蓋 gài is its lid, a noun here. 開蓋／閉蓋 means open/close its lid. The separate preparation also demonstrates opening a chest directly. These are explicit extensions of the earlier container actions; no new passive or general state construction is hidden in them. 扣 kòu is specifically the fastening loop/clasp securing the lid, joining lid and chest. It is not a carrying handle or decorative ring, and the noun does not license the verbs knock, fasten or deduct. The dictionary supports a fastening noun; this exact chest use is an editorial choice for supported graded narration, not a quotation or a claim of attested early Classical terminology.

裂 liè describes a split; 壞 huài describes damage more generally. The large chest's lid is already split. At the end the small chest's lid is not split, but its clasp is. Those are different defects on different chests. 視扣, looking at the clasp, does not identify who caused the break. An hears Ning's call and comes back to inspect; the guest looks at An. The distant teacher has not arrived and cannot already know what happened by direct observation.

The story introduces two indoor rooms and two different doors before any trial. The closed exterior door faces the rain. Ning opens the other door into an adjoining room whose shelf is explicitly dry. In the first room the second room is 彼屋, “that room”; after crossing, speakers may call their current room 此屋, “this room.” Follow the named holder and doorway rather than treating this/that as fixed labels. 門內 means inside the door, not the unstudied compound inner door. No outdoor journey or transfer from the distant household is implied.

箱中無處 means “No placing-spot remains inside this chest” for the waiting material in the current occupied arrangement. This bounded container application extends the earlier shelf-space context; a book occupying the available cargo space makes the limitation explicit. It is not a universal packing theorem, and 存 still means preserve, not can contain. The wet fascicle stays with the reader while the dry first load travels. An returns with the same empty chest before Ning loads the wet fascicle separately. At the end that fascicle is still wet on the dry-room shelf; the reader keeps its wet marked wrapper in the original room. The guest's book and closed case are below the dry shelf, and he holds the lamp and the explicitly removed dry surname sheet. Nothing has instantly dried, repaired itself or proved an owner identity.

C.instruction: Answer each English cue in your own taught Chinese sentences, then compare the model and rubric. Alternative accurate answers are welcome; these are self-checked, not exact-string tests. Numbered questions: 1. Explain the failed trial, distinguishing the two doors.; 2. Name the dry first load and what remains with the reader.; 3. Show the empty return before the second loaded crossing.; 4. Name the second carrier and where the wet fascicle ends.; 5. Track the marked wrapper and the guest sheet at the end.; 6. Name the actual broken fastening and what An observes.
